At today's September event, Apple officially unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo, but did not announce the standard iPhone 18 at the same time. Here's why.

The standard iPhone 18 is expected to launch in early 2027, as Apple has adjusted its new device release schedule.

Generally speaking, today's Apple event would naturally be referred to as the 'iPhone 18 launch event.'

However, Apple's arrangement surprised many people — they did not release the iPhone 18 today, at least not the standard version.

Instead, Apple only unveiled three premium new iPhones this time: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo.

This flagship lineup is clearly different from Apple's past approach: previously, the new standard iPhone would be announced alongside the Pro models at the same time. However, as early as May 2025, there were already reports foreshadowing this change.

According to multiple reports, the three new iPhones Apple launched today will be joined by three more new devices in early 2027:

  • iPhone 18
  • iPhone 18e
  • iPhone Air 2

So the standard iPhone 18 hasn't been cancelled — it's just shipping later than usual.

Why the change?

One explanation is that Apple wants to expand the scale of its iPhone product lineup, adding new models such as the foldable phone Duo, and therefore doesn't want to release too many products all at once in the autumn. Splitting the main iPhone launches into autumn and spring cycles may prove more advantageous.

Another possible reason is that Apple foresaw the current memory shortage early on, knowing that simultaneously launching the standard iPhone 18 along with the Pro and Duo models would make it difficult to meet market demand.

Either way, the iPhone 18 will eventually arrive — just not until early 2027.

What are your thoughts on Apple's strategy of splitting the iPhone 18 series into two separate launch phases? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
